note: Ask these after the demo, in conversation. Do not take notes during the demo. Fill in session_notes_template.json within 15 minutes of finishing. Automatic capture covers what they did; these questions cover what they think.

hypotheses.H1: Lenders will treat a field-verified readiness record as assessable and save effort
hypotheses.H2: A third party can be paid a contingent fee on disbursement without conflict with affordability or licensing
hypotheses.H3: The facilitator will treat readiness as a pipeline output and route cohorts to it
hypotheses.H4: The record carries forward into decisioning and monitoring (the infrastructure claim)
hypotheses.H5: There is a named buyer, owner and path to a pilot

commitment_ladder.label: Names who else must see it
Agrees to discuss a pilot, with a named owner
Commits to a dated pilot step (data, access or approval)

asking_guidance: Ask open questions first. Do not offer options unless the question lists them.
Do not pitch, defend or explain a screen while asking.
Ask the baseline question (B1 or N1) before any question that mentions a Symphony feature.
Record quotes under 20 words, attributed to a role, never a name.
Ask C5 last. Do not suggest a level.
If asked about price, listen and record the response. Do not offer a number unless you have decided to.
Tell attendees at the start that their interactions with the demo are recorded on this device only, with no names.

questions.question: What is the first thing you would change about what you just saw?
questions.listen_for: Specific change requests (signals real consideration) vs generic praise

questions.question: What would stop you using this?
questions.listen_for: Regulatory, process, trust or cost blockers. Note whether any is removable

questions.question: Which screen was most useful to you, and which was least useful?
questions.listen_for: Compare to automatic dwell data (stated vs revealed interest)

questions.question: Who else would need to see this before anything could happen?
questions.listen_for: Roles, not names. Count the number of distinct functions named

questions.question: Where on this ladder would you place the next step you are willing to take?
questions.listen_for: Record the level they choose and what they say to justify it. Do not suggest a level
questions.follow_up: What would have to be true to move one level up?

questions.question: Walk me through what your team does today with a cooperative application like this, from first contact to credit committee. Where does the time go?
questions.listen_for: Hours or days per stage; who does each; where rework happens. This is your baseline, so do not reveal any claim about their process first
questions.follow_up: How many such applications does your team handle per quarter?

questions.question: Looking at the case you were shown, which parts would your team accept as presented, which would they re-verify, and which would they redo?
questions.listen_for: Anything they would 'redo' is a requirement or evidence gap. Anything 'accept' is the value

questions.question: What would your team need to see before relying on evidence verified by a field agent rather than by your own staff?
questions.listen_for: Independence, training, liability, sampling, audit rights. Note any request for a warranty or indemnity

questions.question: If a case arrives in this form, what happens to it inside your organisation? Which functions touch it: credit, risk, compliance, legal?
questions.listen_for: Approval chain. Note whether a policy change is needed

questions.question: How would you want to receive cases like this: through a portal, by email, or into your own systems?
questions.listen_for: Integration burden. Note any security or data-residency requirement

questions.question: Which of the monitoring screens would your team actually use: use of proceeds, covenants, portfolio? Which would replace something you do now?
questions.listen_for: Replacement of an existing process is stronger than 'nice to have'

questions.question: Have you ever paid, or shared a fee with, a party that prepared or referred a borrower? How did that work and what rules applied?
questions.listen_for: Existing precedent, any regulatory limit, who decided. Do not name a fee level yet

questions.question: If a third party were paid when a loan is disbursed, what concerns would you have about incentives, borrower cost or regulation?
questions.listen_for: Conflict-of-interest, affordability, licensing, disclosure to borrower

questions.question: Was anything you were shown something we should not claim, or that could create risk for you?
questions.listen_for: Red flags and wording to change. Treat as high-value

questions.question: What would a pilot need to look like for you to say yes, and who would own it on your side?
questions.listen_for: Scope, size, duration, data access, named owner. Distinguish 'could' from 'would'

questions.question: How do you define and measure readiness for a cohort today? What does a cohort need to show to count as pipeline progress?
questions.listen_for: Their definition and metrics. Compare to the prototype's readiness state

questions.question: Does the readiness record match what you would want a lender to receive? What is missing, and what is extra?
questions.listen_for: Gaps and redundancies in requirements

questions.question: How does technical assistance funding reach enterprises today, and where would a route paid on loan disbursement fit or conflict?
questions.listen_for: Overlap with funded TA, willingness to refer, any policy against success-based fees

questions.question: What would you need before encouraging lenders to treat records like these as assessable?
questions.listen_for: Endorsement path, lender engagement, standards

questions.question: What cohort-level information would you want, how often, and who would you report it to?
questions.listen_for: Reporting cadence and audience. Note donor-facing needs

questions.question: Who else would want the environmental baseline captured at readiness, and for what purpose?
questions.listen_for: Named stakeholders or programmes. Distinguish interest from funding

questions.question: How are cooperatives selected for programmes today, and would a readiness record change selection?
questions.listen_for: Selection criteria. Relevance to choosing the strongest candidates first

questions.question: What would a first cohort pilot require from your side: approvals, timing, constraints?
questions.listen_for: Concrete steps and dates
